title: The Loneliest City

concept.title: Floyd-Warshall: all distances between all pairs of nodes, with three nested loops
body: Sometimes the distance between **every pair** of nodes is needed. Running Dijkstra from every node works, but for small `n` there is a shorter method, the *Floyd-Warshall algorithm*. Let `dist[i][j]` be the length of the best known route from `i` to `j`, at first the length of the road `i - j` (or infinity if none) and 0 for `i = j`. Then try each city `k` as a **stop on the way**: if going through `k` is shorter, use it.

The order of the loops matters: **the stop `k` is the outermost loop**. After round `k`, `dist[i][j]` is the shortest route that uses only the cities `1..k` as stops. The time is O(n^3), fine for `n <= 100` (one million steps).

Here, after computing the distances, count for every city `i` the number of other cities `j` with `dist[i][j] <= t` (the neighbours within the threshold). Print the city with the **fewest** such neighbours; if several cities tie, print the one with the **largest number**.

statement: There are `n` cities and `m` two-way roads with lengths. A city `j` is a neighbour of the city `i` if the shortest route from `i` to `j` (over any roads) has the length at most `t`, `j != i`. Print the city that has the fewest neighbours; if several cities have the same smallest number, print the one with the largest number.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, `m` and `t`: the number of cities, the number of roads and the distance threshold.
Each of the next `m` lines has three numbers `u`, `v` and `w`: a two-way road of length `w` between the cities `u` and `v`.
outputFormat: Print the number of the city.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated roads.

examples.note: City 1 reaches 2 and 3 within 4; city 2 reaches 1, 3 and 4; city 3 reaches 1, 2 and 4; city 4 reaches 2 and 3. The cities 1 and 4 tie with two neighbours; the largest number is 4.

hints: Compute all pairs shortest distances with Floyd-Warshall (the intermediate city is the outer loop).
For each city count the other cities within distance t.
Choose the smallest count; on a tie choose the larger city number.
